sections.title: Constraint Analysis & Conflict Resolution
sections.content:
- **HIGH [INJURY]:** Shoulder/rotator cuff: neutral grip, no behind-neck
  → Injury modification active: Shoulder/rotator cuff: neutral grip, no behind-neck. Exercise selection adjusted.
- **MEDIUM [RECOVERY]:** Stress 5/10: monitor recovery
- **LOW [TRAINING]:** Intermediate: undulating periodization

**Resolution Priority:** Safety > Medical > Injury > Recovery > Nutrition > Training > Adherence > Psychological > Lifestyle

**Coach Note:** Alice's training program must prioritize injury modification due to her pre-existing rotator cuff issue, necessitating the use of neutral grip exercises and avoiding behind-neck movements to minimize strain on her shoulder. This constraint interacts with her moderate stress levels, which require careful monitoring of recovery to avoid exacerbating the injury or hindering progress towards her fat loss goal. As a result, her undulating periodization training approach will need to be carefully calibrated to balance intensity and volume with recovery needs.

sections.title: Program Overview
sections.content:
**Protocol Focus:** Fat Loss-focused programming with Intermediate-appropriate volume landmarks.
**Training Split:** Upper/Lower Split
**Schedule:** 4x/week, 60min sessions
**Phasing:** Two-phase approach
  - Phase 1 (Weeks 1-4): Accumulation & Movement Quality
  - Phase 2 (Weeks 5+): Intensification & Progressive Overload

**Evidence Base:** Informed by 21 decision rules from Muscle OS knowledge vault.

**Coach Note:** For Alice Johnson, the overall program strategy will focus on a calorie-controlled diet with a moderate deficit, paired with a 4-day split resistance training program to maintain muscle mass while promoting fat loss. Given her 2 years of training experience, we'll aim to increase the intensity of her workouts through progressive overload, while also incorporating exercises that avoid exacerbating her old rotator cuff injury. Additionally, we'll prioritize upper body exercises that don't put excessive strain on her shoulders, such as rows and lat pulldowns.

sections.title: Training: Phase 1 — Accumulation & Stability
sections.content:
**Duration:** Weeks 1-4
**Goal:** Accumulation & Movement Quality

### Upper A: Push/Pull Balance
| Exercise | Sets | Reps | RIR | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Dumbbell Bench Press (Neutral Grip) | 3 | 10-12 | 2 | Control tempo 2-0-2 [Shoulder-safe] |
| Lat Pulldown (Neutral Grip) | 3 | 10-12 | 1-2 | Full stretch at top |
| Seated Cable Row | 3 | 12-15 | 1-2 | Squeeze shoulder blades together |
| DB Lateral Raise (Thumb Up) | 3 | 15-20 | 1 | Light weight, strict form [Shoulder-safe] |
| Face Pull (Low Pulley) | 3 | 15-20 | 1 | External rotation focus |

### Lower A: Compound/Glutes
| Exercise | Sets | Reps | RIR | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Goblet Squat | 3 | 10-12 | 2 | Depth control |
| Dumbbell RDL | 3 | 12-15 | 2 | Soft knees, feel stretch |
| Leg Press | 3 | 15-20 | 1 | High volume pump |
| Walking Lunge | 3 | 10/leg | 2 | Control each rep |
| Calf Raise (Standing) | 3 | 15-20 | 1 | Slow, full ROM |

### Upper B: Volume Focus
| Exercise | Sets | Reps | RIR | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Machine Chest Press (Neutral Grip) | 3 | 12-15 | 2 | Controlled 3s negative [Shoulder-safe] |
| Dumbbell Row (Single Arm) | 3 | 10-12/arm | 2 | Supported, full ROM |
| Incline DB Press | 3 | 12-15 | 1-2 | Upper chest focus [Shoulder-safe] |
| Cable Lateral Raise | 3 | 15-20 | 1 | Constant tension [Shoulder-safe] |
| Triceps Pushdown + DB Curl SS | 2 | 12-15 | 1-2 | Superset for density |

### Lower B: Unilateral Focus
| Exercise | Sets | Reps | RIR | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Bulgarian Split Squat | 3 | 10-12/leg | 2 | Stability focus |
| Glute Bridge (Weighted) | 3 | 12-15 | 1-2 | Squeeze at top |
| Hamstring Curl (Machine) | 3 | 12-15 | 1-2 | Controlled negative |
| Hip Flexor Stretch Hold | 2 | 45s/side |  | Post-workout mobility |

sections.title: Training: Phase 2 — Intensification & Progressive Overload
sections.content:
**Duration:** Weeks 5+
**Goal:** Intensification & Progressive Overload

**Progression:** When RIR drops below 2 on all sets of a movement, increase weight 5-7.5% or add 1 set. Re-test MAV landmarks after 8 weeks.

sections.title: Warm-Up & Cool-Down Protocol
sections.content:
### Warm-Up Protocol
5 min incline walk or bike (RPE 3-4)
Dynamic warm-up: leg swings, cat-cow, thoracic rotations, band pull-aparts
Movement-specific warm-up: 2x10 reps at 50% working weight
IPTA warm-up standard: 5-10 min general cardio → dynamic stretching → movement-specific warm-up at 40-60% working weight.

# Injury-Training Compatibility Matrix

For each injury, classifies all major training movements as **Safe (Green)**, **Modified (Yellow — with plane/ROM/load change)**, or **Contraindicated (Red)**. This extends the Default Exercise Pool injury overrides by providing a full-body training classifica

### Cool-Down Protocol
5 min light cardio (RPE 2-3)
Static stretching for worked muscle groups: 30s holds
Optional: foam rolling for tight areas

sections.title: Sleep Protocol
sections.content:
- Target: 7.5-8h consistent bedtime ±30min
- Morning light exposure: 10min outdoor light within 30min of waking
- Screen curfew: No screens 60min pre-bed
- Room temp: 17-19°C
- Pre-bed: 30-40g casein + 200mg magnesium glycinate
- No alcohol within 3h of bedtime

sections.title: Rehab & Prehab
sections.content:
**Shoulder:** Neutral grip pressing, face pulls, external rotation, YTWs. No behind-neck.



**Coach Note:** To address Alice's old rotator cuff injury, I recommend incorporating exercises that strengthen her shoulder stabilizers, such as lateral raises and reverse flys, 2-3 times a week. Additionally, she should focus on proper scapular positioning and engage in regular self-myofascial release techniques, like foam rolling, to maintain optimal shoulder mobility. It's also essential to modify any heavy overhead presses or lifts to avoid exacerbating the injury.

sections.title: Vault-Informed Decisions
sections.content:
The following evidence-based insights influenced this program:

- [Schoenfeld - Science and Development of Muscle Hypertrophy] Per Schoenfeld: longer rest (2-3 min) maintains mechanical tension across sets.
- [Schoenfeld - Science and Development of Muscle Hypertrophy] Per Schoenfeld: prioritize exercises that train target muscles at long lengths under load.
- [Schoenfeld - Science and Development of Muscle Hypertrophy] Per Schoenfeld: deload every 6-8 weeks preventatively — reduce volume 40-60% at same intensity.
- [Schoenfeld - Science and Development of Muscle Hypertrophy] Per Schoenfeld: monitor overreaching — performance decline, mood disturbance, sleep disruption, elevated HR, illness frequency.
- [Jeff Nippard - The Muscle Ladder] Per Nippard: 6-15 reps is the hypertrophy sweet spot — below 6 lacks metabolic stimulus.
- [Jeff Nippard - The Muscle Ladder] Per Nippard: deload every 6-8 weeks preventatively — never wait for exhaustion symptoms.
- [NSCA - Essentials of Strength Training and Conditioning] Per NSCA: load assignment by goal — strength ≥85% 1RM (2-6 reps), hypertrophy 67-85% 1RM (6-12 reps).
- [NSCA - Essentials of Strength Training and Conditioning] Per NSCA: cap volume increase at 20-30% per mesocycle to prevent injury and systemic fatigue.
- [NSCA - Essentials of Strength Training and Conditioning] Per NSCA: 3-tier fatigue — <2w acute (normal), 2-4w functional overreaching (expected supercompensation), >4w nonfunctional (medical).
- [NSCA - Essentials of Strength Training and Conditioning] Per NSCA: 3+ criteria for >4 weeks — performance decline, fatigue, sleep/mood disruption, appetite loss, frequent illness → medical escalation.
- [NSCA - Essentials of Strength Training and Conditioning] Per NSCA: standardized 4-phase warm-up protocol (15-20 min total).
- [NSCA - Essentials of Strength Training and Conditioning] Per NSCA: detraining recovery guidelines — 1-2w off at 90%, 2-4w at 80%, 4-8w at 70%, 8+w at 50-60%.
- [NSCA - Essentials of Strength Training and Conditioning] Per NSCA: female ACL risk 2-8x higher — include landing mechanics, hamstring strength, plyometric progression.
- [ACE - Personal Trainer Manual] Per ACE: first 2 weeks prioritize adherence over optimal — achievable > perfect.
- [ACE - Personal Trainer Manual] Per ACE IFT model: verify pain-free ROM, neutral spine, and 15s single-leg balance before progressing intensity.
- [IPTA - Certified Personal Trainer] Per IPTA: rep range by goal — power (1-5), strength (1-6), hypertrophy (6-12), endurance (12-20+).
- [IPTA - Certified Personal Trainer] Per IPTA: rest by goal — strength 3-5 min, hypertrophy 30-90s, endurance 30-60s.
- [IPTA - Certified Personal Trainer] Per IPTA: 3-phase warm-up — general cardio, dynamic mobility, movement-specific preparation.
- [IPTA - Certified Personal Trainer] Per IPTA: 4-criteria movement screen gate before loaded exercise — ROM, squat, balance, hinge.
- [IPTA - Certified Personal Trainer] Per IPTA: periodization by training status — beginner (linear), intermediate (undulating), advanced (block).
- [IPTA - Bodybuilding Screen] Per IPTA Bodybuilding: recovery priority — sleep > protein > active > passive. Reduce volume first when recovery is compromised.
